payload.name: Preserve-valid-facts-when-updating-memory
payload.description: When performing an UPDATE on an existing memory, preserve all prior facts that remain true and are not contradicted by new evidence; merge or append new information instead of overwriting the memory content.
content: Before updating a memory, review existing content for facts that remain true given the new message; do not assume the new message replaces the entire memory.
When new evidence describes a different event, state, or detail that does not conflict with existing facts, perform an enrichment or merge: keep prior true statements and add new information.
If the update is triggered by a state change, retain past events that are not contradicted and remain part of the subject's history; only modify what the new evidence actually changes.

solves: Updates that rewrite a memory's content with only newly mentioned facts, losing earlier verified facts. The diagnosed cause was an UPDATE triggered by a new health state that replaced a previously stored weekend activity. The rule preserves non-contradicted prior facts by merging new information into existing memory, and applies whenever new evidence describes an additional event, state, or enrichment not conflicting with what is already stored.
